- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 10–15 day average is >10% above recent 30-day mean, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next 5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is volatile, model overreacts to short-term noise; smooth 30-day forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often misreads sentiment; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 days to avoid overconfidence in upside.
- Model tends to overforecast in early 30-day window (days 1–5) when sentiment is positive; cap first 5 days’ forecast at 10% below 10-day moving average.
